reader.notes: With no RECORD clause and 01s of 20 and 6 characters, the file registers as fixed (D-FRA implied Format 1), so REWRITE of the 6-character record stores the full 20-character area. A 1985 program cannot observe this, because the content past a shorter record is undefined and no DEPENDING item exists. Within RECORD VARYING, the replacing length is honoured.

refuter.evidence: Attacked the reader's 'registers as fixed' note. §1985:II.2.1.4.3 makes the choice implementor defined when the RECORD clause is omitted or names a range: OK §1985:II.2.1.4.3 'Where no RECORD clause is specified ... it is implementor defined whether fixed length or variable length records'. The choice is documented in docs/conformance/7/DOC-A.1-147.md (implied format 1, the largest 01) and DOC-A.1-148.md (format 3 is variable). Probes: q1_rw_vary.cob (RECORD IS VARYING 6 TO 20, no DEPENDING, 01s of 20 and 6) gave SHORTER=00 and READ INTO gave [K001TT + 14 spaces]: a 6-character replacing record is stored at 6, and the group move pads it (§1985:VII.3.8.4 GR10b/GR12b, OK). q3_rw_fmt3.cob (RECORD CONTAINS 6 TO 20) gave the same. q2_rw_norec.cob (no RECORD clause) gave [K001TTLLLL...]: the documented fixed choice. q7_rw_odo.cob (ODO, no DEPENDING) rewrote with N=1 -> 00 and READ INTO gave [K0011XX + 5 spaces]; N=0 at the minimum -> 00 (§1985:VII.3.8.4 GR10c, OK). Same results at --std 2023 for q1.
